themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints in CD 403 exploded to 135 THIS WEEK, a 640% spike versus the 8-week baseline of 18.2 weekly complaints (z-score: 26.48), suggesting either a sudden infrastructure failure event or a major pothole/subsidence problem requiring urgent DOT investigation.
evidence: 135 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 18.2 average over prior 8 weeks (640% increase)
Z-score of 26.48 indicates extreme statistical outlier
Aligns with repeated CB budget requests to 'Reconstruct streets' — suggests chronic infrastructure need now acute
reporting_angles: Ground-truth: Map the 135 complaints to identify geographic hotspot (single neighborhood block vs. district-wide)
Interview DOT about whether a specific event triggered the spike—storm damage, utility work, structural failure

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints jumped to 7 THIS WEEK, a 700% spike from the 0.9 weekly average (z-score: 5.82), possibly tied to recent NYC appointment of new 'vendor czar' and the timing of Eid celebrations in the district, suggesting regulatory confusion or enforcement changes.
evidence: 7 mobile food vendor complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average (700% increase, z-score: 5.82)
Gothamist reported NYC named new vendor 'czar' on 2026-03-20—timing overlaps with spike
Documented article on Eid celebrations (2026-03-20) suggests high foot traffic and vendor activity in district
reporting_angles: Contact new vendor czar's office: Are enforcement protocols changing? Have street vending rules or locations shifted?
Interview street vendors in Jackson Heights/Elmhurst about whether they've received new guidance or citations

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal Failures Widespread
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal condition complaints spiked to 92 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 309% increase from the 22.5 weekly baseline (z-score: 7.07), and remain elevated, creating safety risks for pedestrians and drivers across the district and warranting immediate DOT safety audit.
evidence: 92 traffic signal complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 22.5 weekly average (309% increase, z-score: 7.07)
Spike occurred 2 weeks ago, suggesting sustained multi-week failure pattern
Traffic signal condition is #7 highest complaint type overall (501 complaints in 90 days)
reporting_angles: Safety reporting: Obtain DOT incident logs for intersection failures and any accidents during this 2-week window
Interview residents about commute delays, near-misses, or pedestrian safety concerns at major intersections

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Takeover
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints jumped to 4 LAST WEEK, a 1500% spike from the 0.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.66), suggesting either coordinated illegal advertisement campaign or enforcement gap in the district.
evidence: 4 illegal posting complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (1500% increase, z-score: 8.66)
Extremely rare baseline (0.2/week) makes even small absolute numbers statistically extreme
Street sweeping complaints also spiked 1660% last week (11 vs. 0.6 avg)—possible related issue
reporting_angles: Visual reporting: Document the illegal postings—are they political, commercial, or nuisance flyers? Geographic pattern?
DCWP or local precinct: Is there enforcement data on illegal posting arrests or summons?

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Service Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints surged to 11 LAST WEEK, a 1660% spike from the 0.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 10.46), indicating possible Sanitation Department service cuts or route changes affecting neighborhood cleanliness.
evidence: 11 street sweeping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (1660% increase, z-score: 10.46)
Mirrors street condition spike—may indicate combined infrastructure + cleanliness deterioration
Converges with illegal posting surge and street condition crisis in same timeframe
reporting_angles: DSNY operations: Have street sweeping schedules changed, routes been cut, or staffing been reduced in CD 403?
Photo essay: Document street cleanliness in major commercial corridors (Roosevelt Ave, etc.) to show resident perception
